NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4558/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/04/2024 undefined 1.
By way of this Appeal, the Appellant-claimant has challenged the judgment and award dated 18.09.2018 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ahmedabad in M.A.C.P. No.28 of 2009.

The Claim Petition was partly allowed and vide the judgment and award, the claimant was entitled to recover the compensation of Rs.1,97,600/- from the respondent No.2 - the owner of the vehicle, while the Insurance Company came to be exonerated from the liability to pay the compensation to the claimant.
The owner of the vehicle has filed a Cross Objection No.66 of 2019 challenging the order of the learned Tribunal to pay compensation to the claimant.

2. The facts giving rise to the present Appeal can be put succinctly as under :-
On 07.10.2008 in the afternoon at 3.30 p.m., the appellant was walking at Meenabajar, at that time, the respondent No.1 came driving his Rickshaw bearing Registration No.GJ-1-AZ-1473 in a rash and negligent manner, on the wrong side and in full speed and dashed the appellant causing serious injuries to the appellant.

The appellant suffered NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4558/2018 JUDGMENT DATED:
12/04/2024 undefined fracture on the left hand, fracture on the jaw and injuries were also caused on the chest and head.

The appellant was taken to Civil Hospital,
Ahmedabad for primary treatment and thereafter, for further treatment, he was hospitalized at Shilp Orthopedic Hospital, Isanpur, Ahmedabad, where the appellant was operated.
A complaint in this regard was registered at Meghaninagar Police Station as I- C.R. No.248 of 2008.

3. Learned Advocate for the appellant - claimant Mr. Tirth Nayak has submitted that the respondent No.1 driver who has been deleted from the cause title by an order below Exhibit 26 was found negligent in driving the Rickshaw bearing Registration No.GJ-01- AZ-1473 owned by the respondent No.2.
It is further submitted that the vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company - respondent No.3.

The learned Tribunal on submission of the Insurance Company who had placed reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v.
Swaran Singh reported in 2004 ACJ 1 (SC) and had found the driver of the vehicle not holding valid license of driving a NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4558/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/04/2024 Akhileshkumar Rajendrasinh Sinh vs Mrutyunjay Harshnath Sinh Rajputh on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180891623/
2

It is further submitted that the learned Tribunal was required to consider the vehicle as a passenger rickshaw and not as a transport vehicle.

Further, the person was holding a license to drive a rickshaw and hence, it cannot be said that the driver was not holding any valid or effective license in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited reported in (2017) 14 SCC 663
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the license to drive a light motor vehicle would include a license to drive a transport vehicle considering the unladen weight of both the vehicles and therefore, submitted that the license would not require any endorsement for the driving the transport vehicle falling under the Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) Class.

4. Per contra, learned Advocate for the respondent - Insurance Company Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati submitted that the learned Tribunal has rightly considered the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4558/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/04/2024 undefined Swaran Singh (supra).

Learned Advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati has supported the judgment and award of the learned Tribunal to consider the driver of the rickshaw not holding valid license, and stated that the judgment and award is proper in context of Swaran Singh (supra).
5. Having heard the submissions canvassed and on perusing the records of the case, it transpires that the primary contention of the learned Advocates representing the parties is with regard to the validity of the license to drive the rickshaw.
During the course of the trial, Exhibit 60 was produced on record which was the certified copy of the RTO Certificate for the information regarding the driving license.
The information which is produced is with regard to the validity of the non-transport vehicle for the period between 11.09.2006 to 10.09.2026.
The type of vehicle as noted is auto-rickshaw.

The certificate of registration of the vehicle shows the month and year of manufacture as 2006 and the unladen weight as 3580 Kgs. and the type of body is a passenger vehicle having a seating capacity of 4.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4558/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/04/2024 undefined 6.

In the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra), which is in force till date, reference to the definition of LMV was made and it was held in reference to Section 2(21) read with Sections 2(15) and 2(48) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 that a LMV would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed.

The transport vehicle and Omni Bus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 Kgs. would be a LMV and also a motor car or truck or roadroller, "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 Kgs.

It was further held that the holder of the driving license to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in Section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or Omnibus or tractor or roadroller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 Kgs.
7. In view of the decision in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra), here the unladen weight of the vehicle being auto-rickshaw (a passenger vehicle) is below the prescribed weight of 7500 Kgs.

Hence, the driver holding the license to drive the LMV would be competent to drive the transport vehicle whose NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4558/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/04/2024 Akhileshkumar Rajendrasinh Sinh vs Mrutyunjay Harshnath Sinh Rajputh on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180891623/
3

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: undefined weight should not exceed 7500 Kgs.

8. In view of the above judgment in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra), the Insurance Policy would cover the accident and as laid down in the judgment of Mukund Dewangan (supra), the license would not require the endorsement to drive the transport vehicle falling under the LMV Class.
Hence, the Insurance Company would be liable to pay the compensation in view of the above proposition of law.
9. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the Appeal is allowed.
The Insurance Company would be liable to pay the compensation to the claimant.
Hence, in view of the fact, the Cross Objection filed by the owner stands allowed.

10. The learned Tribunal has permitted to recover from the respondent No.2, an amount of Rs.1,97,600/- with rate of interest @ 7.5% per annum, from the date of the claim petition till its realization.

In the result, the present respondent - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the above NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/4558/2018 JUDGMENT DATED: 12/04/2024 undefined amount within a period of EIGHT (8) WEEKS from the date of receipt of writ of the order of this Court.
It is further directed that the claimants would be entitled to receive the compensation with rate of interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of the application.
After deposit of the compensation amount, the entire amount be disbursed to the claimant, after following the necessary procedure for verification of his identity.

11. In view of the above, the Appeal is allowed and the judgment and award dated 18.09.2018 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Ahmedabad in M.A.C.P. No.28 of 2009 stands modified to the above extent.

Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Court /
Tribunal forthwith.
